title: 2000X | Science Fiction Audio Drama
author: Heritage Radio Vault
description:
🚀 You open a door into tomorrow. The world looks familiar. Then the machines stop, time turns against you, and being human becomes the most dangerous thing you can be.

Welcome to 2000X: Tales of the Next Millennia on Heritage Radio Vault, a science fiction audio drama anthology where extraordinary discoveries carry unexpected consequences.

Hosted by Harlan Ellison, this collection brings speculative fiction to life through dramatised adaptations of stories by Ray Bradbury, Robert A. Heinlein, Ursula K. Le Guin, H. G. Wells, Kurt Vonnegut, Octavia E. Butler and other distinctive literary voices.

Enter futures shaped by ambition, invention, rebellion and survival. Meet people confronting impossible choices, societies approaching breaking point and discoveries that change the rules halfway through the game.

The future is waiting. Would you recognise the danger in time?

🎙️ Harlan Ellison at the threshold

Produced by Hollywood Theater of the Ear for NPR, with Yuri Rasovsky as producer and director, 2000X carries the tradition of radio storytelling into the new millennium.

Ellison’s presence introduces a collection willing to question authority, challenge comfortable assumptions and explore what happens when humanity gets exactly what it asked for.

These science fiction and fantasy dramas turn vast ideas into personal encounters. Behind every imagined future is someone with something to lose.

⏳ Time travel, dangerous technology and worlds beyond our own

Across the original series, discover stories such as:

🌀 By His Bootstraps, Robert A. Heinlein

Step into a time travel puzzle where cause and consequence refuse to stay in order.

⚙️ The Machine Stops, E. M. Forster

Enter a society dependent on technology and confront the terrifying possibility that its foundations could fail.

🔥 Pillar of Fire, Ray Bradbury

Encounter a future whose treatment of the past raises disturbing questions about fear, memory and imagination.

⏰ “Repent, Harlequin!” Said the Ticktockman, Harlan Ellison

Discover a world ruled by punctuality, where defiance means putting your own remaining time at risk.

Browse the available episodes and choose the idea that unsettles you most.

🎭 Hear the moment everything changes

A voice hesitates. An explanation falls apart. Someone realises the system they trusted has no intention of protecting them.

Through performance and sound, 2000X makes its imagined worlds immediate. Listen for the human stakes beneath the invention, the fear behind the discovery and the choice that cannot be taken back.

Each story offers a different way into the collection. Begin with a favourite author, follow an intriguing title or let an unfamiliar voice lead you somewhere unexpected.

🏆 Science fiction with an award-winning legacy

2000X: Tales of the Next Millennia received the Ray Bradbury Award, recognising the work of Harlan Ellison and Yuri Rasovsky.

For fans of science fiction radio drama, time travel stories, dystopian fiction, literary adaptations and immersive audio theatre, 2000X offers stories that give your imagination somewhere extraordinary to go.

🎧 Choose a story. Cross the threshold. Discover what tomorrow might cost.

🔔 Follow 2000X on Heritage Radio Vault and keep another possible future within reach.

F*CK! I’M 50 started with a pretty simple question: where the bloody hell did the last 20 years go?


One minute you’re busy working, raising kids and dealing with life, the next you wake up and realise — F*CK! I'm 50! Our kids hardly need us anymore, yet our parents need us more than ever before.


My name's Paul Burfitt. My mates call me Burf. I’m not a guru, not a life coach and certainly not an expert. I’m just a bloke from Queensland who’s decided I’m not going to keep putting everything off.


So I’m talking to people from around Australia and other places about all the stuff that comes up at this stage of life — family, money, health, work, relationships, ambitions, regrets, f*ck-ups, starting again and figuring out what makes you happy.


Some conversations will be with everyday people who have great stories. Others will be with people you already know from sport, media, business or somewhere completely unexpected. And every now and then I’ll bring in someone who genuinely knows a thing or two on the subject they’re talking.


I’ve got a podcast and a little YouTube channel set up. You’re invited to come along for the ride as I start ticking off a few things I’ve spent too many years saying I’d do “one day”.


I'm sure some people will think it's a brilliant idea. Plenty more probably won’t. But either way here we go, and remember this is a hate free zone so play nice…

There's sure to be some spills, thrills and the occasional disaster as I try to make up for a bit of lost time.


If the name of my show is a bit in your face - that's kind of the point - you can always refer to it as Fi50 too.


Most of all remember, F*CK! I’M 50 isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about finally asking the questions — and doing something about them.

title: Morning Farm Sounds (500 episodes)
author: Robin Verrue
description:
Morning Farm Sounds brings you real farm ambience from the first light of day: cows lowing, sheep and goats bleating, pigs grunting, horses nickering, hens clucking, a rooster crowing, ducks quacking, geese honking and wild birdsong, all together in one calm, living soundscape. No music, no talking, no host. Just a farm waking up.


Every episode is a 10 to 13 minute recording of a real working farm in the morning, made from our own recordings with permission. You hear the real thing: real animals going about their morning, no synthetic loops, no sound effects and never animals in distress. Only calm, everyday farm sounds.


Why farm sounds?

Rain and white noise are steady, but a farm is alive. The natural, irregular voices of farm animals give your ears gentle variety without ever asking for your attention. Many listeners find that this makes farm ambience a wonderful background for concentration, rest and slowing down, a short escape to the countryside wherever you are.


Why 10 to 13 minutes?

Each episode is made to fit into a real day. It's long enough to settle in and short enough to press play anytime: a focus sprint, a study session, a screen break, a power nap or a short meditation.


Use Morning Farm Sounds for:

- Deep focus and concentration while you work

- Studying, revision and exam preparation

- Calm and relaxation after a busy moment

- A 10-minute work break or screen break

- Reading with a cup of coffee or tea

- A gentle, grounded morning routine

- A short nap or power nap

- Meditation, mindfulness and breathwork


What you will hear:

- Cows lowing and mooing

- Sheep bleating

- Goats bleating and calling

- Pigs grunting softly

- Horses snorting, nickering and whinnying

- Hens clucking

- A rooster crowing at dawn

- Ducks quacking

- Geese honking

- Wild birdsong


Each morning is different: dawn, sunrise, first light, daybreak, early morning and mid-morning. The voices rise and fall in their own time, each episode starts and ends gently, so you can play them back to back or on repeat without a jolt. A speaker works well; headphones make the farm feel close enough to touch.


Common questions:

Is this a real farm? Yes. Every episode is built from our own recordings of farm animals, made with permission.

Is there music or talking? No. No music, no host, no announcements and no identifiable voices, just the farm.

Are the animals calm? Yes. We only use calm, everyday morning sounds. You will never hear animals in distress.

Will the rooster wake me up? The rooster crows now and then as part of the morning, which makes these episodes perfect for a gentle start, a focus session or a short rest, rather than a full night's sleep.

Can I loop it? Yes. Each episode fades in and out softly.


Made for adults who love real nature sounds, countryside ambience, cottagecore mornings and slow living. This is not a children's learning program with labels or narration, just honest, peaceful farm sounds for grown-up days.


A new farm morning every day. Follow Morning Farm Sounds so you never miss an episode, and if the farm helps you focus, rest or relax, a 5-star rating on Spotify or Apple Podcasts really helps the show grow.


You might also enjoy our other shows: Relaxing Raindrops, The Purring Podcast and Mountain Wind Sounds.


Farm sounds, farm animal sounds, morning farm ambience, barnyard sounds, rooster crowing, countryside sounds, nature sounds for focus, study and relaxation. No music, no talking.

title: Law of Attraction Secrets
author: Law of Attraction Secrets
description:
What if the way you think about your day quietly shapes the way you experience it? Law of Attraction Secrets is a podcast of short, focused idea-episodes about thought, attention, and mindset. Each episode takes one simple idea, looks at it from a few angles, and leaves you with something to reflect on as you go about your life. No hype, no shortcuts, and no promises of instant change. Just clear, calm conversations about the inner side of everyday living.
WHAT THIS SHOW IS ABOUT
The phrase "law of attraction" means different things to different people. For some, it suggests a mysterious force. For others, it is simply a reminder that what we focus on tends to grow in our awareness. This show leans toward the practical and reflective end of that spectrum. We explore the idea that our thoughts, expectations, and habits of attention influence how we interpret events, which opportunities we notice, and how we respond when things do not go as planned.
Rather than treating attraction as a formula, we treat it as a lens. Through that lens, we ask useful questions. What am I paying attention to right now? What story am I telling myself about this situation? Which beliefs are guiding my choices without my noticing? These questions do not have one correct answer, and that is exactly why they are worth asking. The aim is not to control the world with our minds, but to become more aware of how our minds meet the world.
Every episode stands on its own. You do not need any background knowledge, special vocabulary, or previous episodes to follow along. You only need a few minutes and a willingness to think honestly about your own experience. Some ideas will resonate with you immediately. Others may feel unfamiliar at first and make more sense weeks later, when a situation in your life brings them back to mind.

HOW SHORT IDEA EPISODES WORK
Law of Attraction Secrets is built around short episodes, each centered on a single theme. One day we might look at the difference between wishing and intending. Another day we might explore why gratitude changes the texture of an ordinary afternoon, or how a single worried thought can grow into a whole imagined future. The format is deliberately compact, so you can listen during a commute, a walk, a coffee break, or the quiet minutes before sleep.
A typical episode moves through three simple steps. First, we introduce the idea in plain language. Second, we connect it to familiar situations: conversations at work, decisions at home, moments of doubt, moments of hope. Third, we offer a reflection question or a small practice you can try on your own. There is no homework and no pressure. The practice is an invitation, not an assignment.
Short episodes have a quiet advantage. Big ideas are often easier to absorb in small pieces. When a concept is presented briefly and clearly, it tends to stay with you longer. You may find yourself remembering a phrase or a question at an unexpected moment, and that moment of remembering is often where the real reflection begins.
THOUGHTS, ATTENTION, AND EVERYDAY LIFE
Much of what we call mindset is really a pattern of attention. Two people can walk down the same street and notice completely different things. One sees closed shops and grey skies; the other sees a friendly face, a new café, an interesting building. Neither is wrong. They are simply looking through different filters. This show spends a lot of time on those filters: where they come from, how they shape our mood, and how we can gently adjust them.
We look at everyday moments where thought and experience meet. The morning thought that sets the tone for the whole day. The habit of rehearsing difficult conversations before they happen. The tendency to expect disappointment so that we will not be surprised by it. The way a small success can change how we approach the next challenge. These are ordinary experiences, but they carry a lot of weight. Understanding them a little better can make daily life feel more intentional and less automatic.
It is important to say clearly what this show does not claim. Thinking positively does not make difficulties disappear, and no one is to blame for hardship simply because of their thoughts. Life includes loss, uncertainty, and circumstances far outside our control. What we explore here is the space we do have: how we pay attention, how we interpret what happens, and how we choose our next step. That space is often larger than we assume, and it is worth exploring with patience and honesty.
THE INNER HABITS WE EXPLORE
Across the episodes, a number of recurring themes appear. One is clarity: the practice of knowing what you actually want, rather than only what you want to avoid. It sounds simple, yet many of us spend more energy describing our fears than describing our hopes. Another is expectation: how our assumptions about what is likely to happen influence how we prepare, how we show up, and how we read the results.
We also explore gratitude, not as a forced exercise, but as a way of noticing what is already present and working. We look at self-talk, the inner voice that comments on everything we do, and how its tone can be softened without becoming dishonest. We spend time on patience, because meaningful change in habits and perspective usually unfolds slowly. We talk about letting go, which is different from giving up: it is the ability to hold an intention while releasing the need to control every detail.
Other episodes focus on visualization and imagination, the way we picture possible futures and how those pictures can either motivate us or overwhelm us. We discuss emotional awareness, recognizing feelings as signals rather than commands. We look at consistency, the small daily choices that quietly add up over time. And we return often to curiosity, perhaps the most useful inner habit of all, because it keeps us open to learning rather than stuck in fixed conclusions about ourselves and others.
WHO THIS IS FOR
This podcast is for anyone who is curious about the connection between inner life and outer experience. You might be new to the idea of the law of attraction and want a grounded, sensible introduction. You might have explored the topic before and want a calmer, more reflective perspective than the dramatic claims you sometimes encounter. Or you might simply enjoy short episodes that make you pause and think.
Listeners often include people going through transitions: starting a new job, moving to a new place, ending or beginning a relationship, or simply feeling that it is time for a fresh outlook. Others are students, creatives, parents, entrepreneurs, and professionals who want a few minutes of mental clarity in a busy day. You do not need to share any particular belief system to benefit. If you are open to examining your own thoughts with kindness and honesty, you are in the right place.
This show is also for skeptics. Healthy questioning is welcome here. You are encouraged to test every idea against your own experience, keep what is helpful, and set aside what is not. Reflection works best when it is personal and honest, not when it is accepted without thought.
HOW TO LISTEN AND USE THESE IDEAS
There is no right way to listen, but a few suggestions may help. Try choosing one episode and letting it be your theme for the day. Notice when the idea shows up in your conversations, your reactions, or your choices. You might write down the reflection question and return to it in the evening. Some listeners keep a simple notebook of ideas that stood out, which over time becomes a personal record of how their thinking has shifted.
It can also help to revisit episodes. An idea that sounded abstract the first time may feel very concrete after a challenging week. Because the episodes are short, replaying one is easy, and repetition often reveals details you missed. Feel free to share episodes with friends or family and talk about them together. Conversation is one of the best ways to turn an interesting idea into a lived understanding.
Above all, go at your own pace. These ideas are meant to support reflection, not to create pressure or unrealistic expectations. Results from any mindset practice vary from person to person, and no single approach fits everyone. Treat each episode as a small conversation with yourself, an opportunity to notice, question, and choose a little more consciously. Subscribe, press play when you need a moment of perspective, and see which ideas become your own.
Law of Attraction Secrets is educational and reflective — not a substitute for professional advice.

title: GS1 Standards and RFID in Healthcare
author: GS1
description:
In this podcast, GS1 experts and healthcare leaders from the UK, Denmark, and Norway explore how RFID, powered by GS1 standards, improves traceability, efficiency, and patient safety.


Henrik Stilling is a Special Advisor in IT Architecture at the Central Denmark Region, where he leads architecture initiatives focused on logistics and identification. With extensive experience implementing RFID solutions at Aarhus University Hospital, Henrik brings practical insights into how automated tracking, GS1 standards and data-driven processes can improve hospital logistics, resource utilisation and operational efficiency.


Rachael Ellis is the Scan for Safety Programme Director at Hull University Teaching Hospitals in the UK. She has led one of the country's largest healthcare RFID implementations, supporting the tracking and management of more than 70,000 hospital assets. With hands-on experience in digital transformation, traceability and clinical operations, Rachael shares valuable insights into the practical challenges and benefits of implementing RFID in healthcare.


Bjørn Ravnestad is an advisor specialising in standards and healthcare technology, supporting public healthcare organisations in Norway. His work focuses on integrating RFID and other tracking technologies into hospital infrastructure, particularly in new hospital construction projects. Bjørn brings valuable experience in asset tracking, GS1 standards and the development of scalable solutions that support more efficient and connected healthcare services.

We take complex concepts and break them down into clear, engaging stories that are easy to understand without sacrificing the fascinating details that make science so powerful. description:
Women of a Certain Strength

Stronger than sterotypes. Too strong to sit this one out!

Who says getting older means slowing down?


Women of a Certain Strength is a podcast celebrating women who refuse to let age define what they can accomplish. We're women over 50 who are still setting goals, lifting heavy, chasing personal records, stepping into fitness competitions, and discovering just how strong we can become.


We're here to talk about all things strength, fitness, competition and conquering gym intimidation to building confidence, navigating the challenges of getting older, and laughing at ourselves along the way, we're keeping it real, relatable and unapologetically honest.


Whether you're a seasoned competitor a weekend warrrior, a gym newbie, or a woman who's been thinking about trying somthing outside her comfort zone, this show is for you!


Expect honest conversations, plenty of laughs, a little friendly competition, stories of triumph and failure, and encouragement to stop waiting for the perfect time to start.


Becuse we're not trying to be 25 again. We're too busy becoming the strongest versions of ourselves right now.


Age is not a finish line.  Strength has no expiration date. And our next chapter might just be our strongest yet


Welcome to Women of a Certain Strength!

description:
Welcome to Seasons of Becoming with Samantha!


A space for real conversations, mindful moments, and navigating the beautiful, messy, exhausting, and sometimes overwhelming parts of life.


Because let's be real, life doesn't always go according to plan. Between motherhood, relationships, careers, personal growth, and everything in between, we're all just trying to figure things out as we go.


I'm Samantha, a Registered Yoga Teacher, meditation teacher in training, MSW student, wife, mom, and someone who's learning to embrace life's many seasons right alongside you.


Here, we'll talk about the things we don't always say out loud. The guilt, the uncertainty, the pressure to have it all together, the unexpected changes, and the moments that make us question what's next.


Some episodes will be guided meditations. Others will feel more like sitting down with a friend over coffee, having an honest conversation about life. And sometimes, it'll be a little bit of both.


My hope is that you'll leave each episode feeling a little more grounded, a little less alone, and reminded that you don't need to have everything figured out.

description:
Build Noet | Where Fantasy Meets Faith, Science, and Imagination


What does it take to build an entire world from the ground up?


Welcome to Build Noet, a creative journey into the making of Noet, an epic science-fantasy novel by author C.B. Hedlun.


Set on a distant world beneath the light of a red dwarf star, Noet explores identity, survival, power, faith, and the struggle to discover one's purpose. Through intricate civilizations, ancient conflicts, unfamiliar landscapes, and characters shaped by their histories, a fictional universe begins to take shape.


But Build Noet is about more than writing a novel. It's about discovering the connections between storytelling, science, history, psychology, theology, and the human experience.

Experience the story as it unfolds. Follow along with narrated readings of Noet as each new chapter is written and released. Rather than waiting for the completed novel, listeners are invited to experience the developing adventure, meet its characters, explore its mysteries, and witness the story come to life one chapter at a time.


Then step Behind the Pages with C.B. Hedlun to discover the research, creative decisions, unexpected discoveries, and spiritual reflections that influence the development of the Noet universe. From planetary environments and evolutionary biology to cultural systems, religious symbolism, and character development, each episode explores how imagination becomes a believable world.


Along the way, discover how seemingly unrelated ideas connect to reveal deeper patterns within a story and how the process of creating fiction can lead to unexpected discoveries about our own world.


Whether you're a fantasy reader, an aspiring writer, a curious explorer, or someone who enjoys discovering the deeper meaning behind a story, Build Noet invites you to experience both the adventure and the creative journey that brings it to life.


Every world has a story. Every civilization has a history. Every character has an identity to discover.


Welcome to Build Noet, where imagination is only the beginning.

description: Real CTOs. Real Privacy Challenges. Real Engineering Solutions. Cue eye-roll. Technically Compliant is the podcast where CTOs talk about what privacy compliance really looks like when you're shipping code, managing legacy systems, and trying to convince the CEO (and yourself) that a consent management platform isn't optional. Each episode, I sit down with CTOs who've been in the trenches—the ones who've retrofitted privacy into monoliths held together with duct tape, discovered entire tables of unexpected PII, survived their first DSAR that returned 80,000 records, and lived to tell the tale of explaining to their CEO why they can't "just ignore the risk." No vendors. No legalese. Just real conversations about the messy reality of building privacy into software that's already moving at full speed (or higher). Because let's be honest: you're probably technically compliant. The question is what happens when someone checks.

description:
What happens when someone finally fights for you?


That question sits at the heart of Carried Through, a podcast about evidence-based patient advocacy, health equity, and the tools every patient deserves but most never receive.


Dr. Valencia Hood-Humphrey, DrPH, MSc, BCPA, is a Doctor of Public Health, a scholar-practitioner in evidence-based practice and implementation science, and a Board Certified Patient Advocate. As Founder & CEO of Insightful Doc™ Consulting, LLC, she brings extensive experience across biopharmaceutical quality, regulatory, and medical affairs. She knows how the system builds treatments from the inside, and exactly where it loses sight of the person waiting for them.


Before she was a scientist, an industry professional, or a patient advocate, Dr. Valencia was a child who was misdiagnosed. What was dismissed as a stomach virus became a ruptured appendix, emergency surgery, and an uncertain prognosis. She remembers her father carrying her through the emergency room doors.

Carried Through: Evidence, Advocacy and the Fight for Every Patient is for patients, families, and communities who deserve both the evidence and someone in their corner.

Through signs, miracles, teachings, and encounters, Jesus reveals Himself as the Bread of Life, the Light of the World, the Good Shepherd, the Resurrection and the Life, and the Way, the Truth, and the Life.At the heart of the Gospel is God's immense love for humanity, expressed through the sacrifice of His Son. We lose people. Jobs end. Relationships change. Businesses fail. We grieve, start again, get older, change direction - and sometimes simply getting through the day is an achievement.

These aren't stories about pretending everything happens for a reason, being relentlessly positive or telling you to "be resilient".


They're honest stories about grief, work, parenthood, relationships, identity, failure, change, hope and starting again.

Some of the stories are Lou's.

Others will come from people who have their own I KEPT GOING story to tell.


Because sometimes keeping going is extraordinary.

And sometimes it's incredibly ordinary.


The dream is simple:

To make people feel acknowledged enough to believe they still have a choice about what happens next.

What if you could explore a map by listening to it?

On Episode 293 of The Geoholics, we sit down with Brandon Biggs, founder and CEO of XR Navigation and creator of Audiom, to talk about making digital maps accessible through sound. Brandon shares how users can explore, draw, and edit maps without relying on sight—and how sonification could help reveal geospatial patterns in a whole new way.

We also get into what accessibility means for surveyors, GIS professionals, and public agencies: from collecting and structuring data in the field to designing and testing maps with disabled users from the start. And we put the future of accessible mapping to the test with our “Bullsh*t, Breakthrough, or Too Soon to Tell?” round.

Tune in for a conversation about technology, inclusion, and building maps that work for more people.

description:
The Dragon's Secret by Augusta Huiell Seaman.  
"The Dragon's Secret" by Augusta Huiell Seaman is a mystery novel likely written in the early 20th century. The story revolves around Leslie Crane, a young girl who is staying with her aunt in a secluded bungalow by the ocean. As Leslie experiences the beauty and excitement of the autumn coast, a series of mysterious events begin to unfold, particularly concerning an adjacent closed bungalow named Curlew's Nest and a peculiar casket associated with it. At the start of the narrative, Leslie enjoys a stormy night at the beach with her dog Rags, leading to an intriguing encounter with a mysterious light at Curlew's Nest. Following this incident, she discovers driftwood and various flotsam on the beach, including a hidden burlap sack containing a beautifully crafted metal box adorned with dragon imagery. The surface of the story hints at secrets and potential adventures as Leslie teams up with another girl, Phyllis, who becomes a friend and accomplice, as they delve deeper into the enigma of the box and its connection to their surroundings. The opening chapters establish not only the setting but also the tone of youthful curiosity and camaraderie that drives the unfolding mystery.

Dalla scuola al mondo del lavoro, il racconto mette al centro l'ascolto, le relazioni e la capacità di costruire comunità più inclusive, resilienti e orientate al futuro.

Ogni puntata affronta temi cruciali: il disagio giovanile e l'esperienza di Scuola in Ascolto, che in tre anni ha promosso oltre 9.000 colloqui con psicologi dedicati a studenti, genitori e formatori; il benessere organizzativo e le 60 buone pratiche raccolte nel Libro Bianco promosso dall'Assessorato al Lavoro di Regione Lombardia, nato per valorizzare esperienze virtuose e diffondere modelli capaci di migliorare la qualità della vita dei lavoratori; il progetto Lombardia per le Donne, che sostiene il rientro al lavoro dopo la maternità attraverso un contributo fino a 400 euro destinato alle neomamme per l'accesso a servizi di baby sitting e assistenza familiare, favorendo un migliore equilibrio tra vita privata e professionale.

Il vodcast approfondisce inoltre il ruolo delle politiche attive del lavoro, le competenze richieste da un mercato in continua evoluzione, l'impatto dell'intelligenza artificiale sui processi produttivi e sulle professioni, e le sfide che imprese, istituzioni e cittadini sono chiamati ad affrontare.

Attraverso il confronto con esperti, rappresentanti delle istituzioni, imprese, professionisti e testimoni diretti, Il fattore umano racconta un'idea di innovazione che non si misura solo con i numeri o con la tecnologia, ma con la capacità di mettere le persone al centro delle scelte, creando opportunità, benessere e valore per l'intera società. description:
A delegation of curious aliens has arrived on Earth with an ambitious goal: launching the galaxy’s first interstellar hotel brand. There is one problem. They have no idea how human hospitality works, starting with hospitality itself and ending with the baffling language of hospitality technology: MCP, RAG, GEO, agentic AI, attribute-based selling, and the rest of the buzzwords everyone nods along to without quite explaining.


To solve that problem, they abducted Simone Puorto. His release depends on one condition: he must teach them everything there is to know about the industry. Since no one can explain it all alone, each episode Simone calls on the people who actually build and run this business to explain a single concept, in language that an alien, or anyone encountering it for the first time, could follow. There is one rule: if the aliens do not understand it, the explanation is not good enough, and Simone stays where he is.


The result is a conversation built for hoteliers, revenue managers, marketers, and operations teams who are tired of hearing the latest buzzword without ever getting a straight answer on what it actually means.

description:
Welcome to Liomugai, the podcast dedicated to the Way of the Sword, Budō, and the Zen of training.


Liomugai ("without borders") is an invitation to explore traditional Japanese martial arts through the eyes of a lifelong student.

This audio journal bridges modern athletic performance and the discipline of Budo—where technical efficiency meets spiritual asceticism, and physical rigor leads to mental peace.


In each episode, dive into the history, practice, and mindset of Mugai-ryū Iaido and martial arts. From technical breakdowns of katas and tameshigiri to reflections on travel and Japanese culture, we explore the concept of Ken Zen Ichi Nyo (The sword and Zen are one) alongside martial philosophies like Reigyo and In-Yō.


About the Host: The podcast is hosted and produced by Lionel Reynaud. A former elite cycling coach on the World Tour and at the Olympic Games (Beijing, London, Rio), he now applies the science of athletic performance to traditional arts. An Okinawan Uechi-Ryu Karate teacher holding a 4th-degree black belt (Yondan) and the title of Jun-Shihan, he is internationally recognized by the IUKF. As a Senior Instructor at the Mattson Academy and founder of the Uechi-Ryu Institute (Kenkyujo), Lionel draws on his journey across France, the United States, and Japan to connect practitioners of all backgrounds.

Whether you are a Budo practitioner, passionate about samurai culture, or simply curious to discover a discipline of self-perfection, join this quest for self-mastery.


🌐 Resources and articles: https://liomugai.com 📱 Follow the training in Japan: Instagram: @liomugai • YouTube: @liomugai


⚠️ Safety Warning: The content of this podcast is shared for informational and cultural purposes. Sword practice is demanding and potentially dangerous. Never attempt to replicate these techniques without the supervision of a qualified instructor in a recognized Dojo.

title: Secret Agent K7
author: Entertainment Radio
description: These fifteen minute episodes of mystery and espionage from the 1939 broadcasts begin with a prolonged organ intro so the local announcer could get in a couple of commercials for the local furniture store or dairy! Each single episode lasted about 12 and 1/2 minutes, but each "case" is really quite interesting and exciting. Walter PidgeonAgent K-7 is actually a rather mild-mannered narrator of these stories. He doesn't sound or seem very heroic or interesting... which would make him all the more effective as a spy! The spy's best disguise is a perfectly ordinary and uninteresting demeanor. The radio actors who brought these stories of men and women operatives to the radio are as unknown today as most of the real spies of that time. The stories are drawn from the headlines and fears of 1939 (and now?) Here are a few examples. "Suicide Ships," "Fortified Borders," "Poisonous Gas," "Undesirable Aliens," "Fraudulent Passports," "Secrets Leaked," "Government Overthrow," and "World Crisis." Sounds like current events. "Exactly the kind of activity that a spy would take advantage of," to quote agent Z. The fine actor Walter Pigeon plays Agent Z in some of the episodes
